extracted.intended_audience: Potential applicants to the U.S. Department of Energy Vehicle Technologies Office (VTO) funding opportunities (researchers, companies, and small businesses preparing NOFO/FOA applications)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting concept papers and full applications in response to Vehicle Technologies Office (VTO) Notices/Funding Opportunity Announcements, including required components, budget justification, and reviewer-focused strengths. Applicable to DOE NOFO/FOA applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance market acceptance / high impact projects
rubrics_metrics.description: EERE supports high impact projects that can significantly and swiftly advance market acceptance of next generation energy efficiency and renewable energy technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should focus on projects with potential for significant and rapid market impact; alignment with EERE’s mission is implied for eligibility and competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check official solicitation notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Official notices of solicitations can be found at the EERE Program Information Center or Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the official sources for authoritative NOFO/FOA documents and updates; the table on this page is informational and may not be inclusive of all solicitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet concept paper and full application deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding opportunities have specified concept paper deadlines and full application deadlines (e.g., concept paper Deadline, Full Application Deadline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must submit by the listed deadlines for the specific FOA/NOFO; funding amounts and schedule dates are subject to change, so monitor official notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the NOFO application phases
rubrics_metrics.description: NOFO process includes concept paper and full application phases; Session 1 provides an overview of these phases and the application process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize yourself with what is required at each phase (what belongs in a concept paper vs full application) and plan submissions accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read and follow specific NOFO language closely
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenters discuss key content to read and review, and specific language to pay close attention to in the NOFO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully follow wording and requirements in the NOFO/FOA; deviations or omissions can affect eligibility/review. Some earlier materials may reference 'FOA' terminology now updated to 'NOFO'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare a complete Budget Justification and required budget forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Application components corresponding to a project budget include SF-424, allowable project costs, Budget Justification, and Cost Share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Session 2 guidance: include required forms (e.g., SF-424), clearly justify allowable costs, document any cost share commitments, and follow examples for best practice when preparing the Budget Justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate allowable project costs and cost share compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Know what project costs are allowable and how cost share is to be documented and justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear evidence and calculations for allowable expenses and how required cost share will be met; follow NOFO-specific cost share rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemble a credible project team and supporting letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Application components include basic information about a project team and letters of commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include team qualifications, roles, and formal letters of commitment or support to demonstrate partner capabilities and commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a Statement of Project Objectives (SOPO)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SOPO is a required element describing project objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly and concisely describe project objectives, deliverables, and measurable outcomes in the SOPO as required by the NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply reviewer-focused strengths (technical review criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Session 3 identifies what makes an application strong from a reviewer’s perspective and identifies strengths and weaknesses based upon VTO’s Technology Integration Program’s technical review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examples from Session 3 to emphasize elements reviewers value (e.g., clarity of technical approach, feasibility, impact, team capability). Address common weaknesses and tailor the application to the explicit technical review criteria for the relevant program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use information session recordings and presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: VTO provides recorded videos and presentations explaining NOFO process and application components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch Sessions 1–3 (and prior years' recordings) for detailed explanations, examples, and tips; note some references may be out of date due to FOA→NOFO terminology change but much content remains relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business applicants: SBIR/STTR intellectual property and commercialization expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR and STTR programs target small businesses, which keep the rights to any technology developed and are encouraged to commercialize it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small business applicants should be prepared to pursue commercialization, retain rights to technology, and understand program-specific expectations for IP and commercialization plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor funding amounts and schedules for changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding amounts and schedule dates are subject to change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly check official notices (EERE Program Information Center, Grants.gov) and NOFO updates to confirm current funding levels and deadlines.
